description: Quick analyst notes for live result race pages.
instructions: Each race id goes under races.
Use raceKey below to see which race each id belongs to.
Put the newest note first; only the first note displays fully.
If you add another note after an existing note, put a comma after the previous note's closing brace.
Allowed note fields: date, author, role, text, image, embed.
Use either image or embed, not both, for simplicity.
Image can be a URL string or an object like { "url": "https://...", "alt": "Short description", "caption": "Optional caption", "size": "small" }.

Embed can be a URL string, an external embed object like { "url": "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=...", "title": "Optional title", "caption": "Optional caption", "height": 320, "size": "small" }, or an internal forecast object like { "type": "governor-race-preview", "state": "CA", "title": "California governor forecast" }.
Supported external embed links match article embeds: YouTube, Vimeo player, Google Docs/Drive, Datawrapper, Flourish, and Observable.
Authors named FEA Analysis Desk, Federal Elections Analysis, Nathan Wang, or gamerdoglover automatically get their saved profile image.

79777.author: gamerdoglover
79777.text: California uses a nonpartisan primary system, where the top two candidates advance to general election. Xavier Becerra currently leads in polling against the second runner-up, Steve Hilton, who is endorsed by Donald Trump. Billionaire and 2020 Presidential Candidate Tom Steyer also holds third place. Well Democrats have the possibility to lock Republicans out of the race, if Steve Hilton advances to general, the forecast largely favors Democrats in the deep blue state.

79778.author: Nathan Wang
79778.text: California uses a nonpartisan primary system, where the top two candidates advance to general election. State Treasurer Fiona Ma is the Democratic frontrunner in the race to replace outgoing Lieutenant Governor Eleni Kounalakis, who is running for Treasurer. Other candidates drawing large support in this race are Democrats Josh Fryday, Michael Tubbs, Oliver Ma and Republicans Gloria Romero and David Fennell.
